mainTopic: Eating food with third-degree impurity (שלישי): when it makes a person's body impure for קודש or unfit for תרומה
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier ruling: being careful at the level of תרומה still counts as impure when it comes to קודש. רבי זירא then reports, through a chain of sages, a ruling of רבי ינאי. If someone eats a שלישי of חולין that were handled with the purity of קודש, his body becomes a שני for קודש. רבי זירא challenges this from a משנה that mentions only the purity of תרומה. רבי אסי answers that the משנה uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style, and the גמרא finally explains that רבי אסי and רבה בר בר חנה disagree about רבי יוחנן's view. Next, עולא rules that eating a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה disqualifies a person from eating תרומה. The גמרא shows why עולא's rule was needed even though the משנה seems to hint at it. Finally, רב המנונא challenges עולא from a משנה that allows a שלישי to be eaten in a stew mixed with תרומה. עולא begins to answer by setting the stew case aside, and his reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous ruling: the purity level of תרומה counts as impure for קודש
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a ruling from the previous discussion. Someone careful only at the level of תרומה is still treated as impure for קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: …is impurity with regard to sacred food.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the previous discussion. Being careful at the level of תרומה purity still counts as impure when it comes to קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set a higher bar for קודש than for תרומה. So a person or food that is 'pure' by the standards of תרומה is treated as impure when dealing with קודש. This sets the background for the next ruling, which is about food handled with the stricter purity of קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
Sacred, consecrated food or items (קודש)

phrases.english: is impurity with regard to sacred food.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: the purity level of תרומה still counts as impure for קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Purity kept at the level of תרומה is still treated as impurity for קודש.

steps.title: Eating a third-degree item of חולין handled with קודש purity makes the body a second-degree for קודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי rules that חולין handled with the purity standards of קודש can become a שלישי. Someone who eats such food becomes a שני for קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ינאי: One who eats third-degree impure non-sacred food that was prepared with the purity of sacred food, his body becomes second-degree impure for sacred food.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is given. If ordinary food was handled with the purity rules of קודש and became a שלישי, a person who eats it becomes a שני for קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, plain חולין cannot become a שלישי at all; impurity stops at שני. But when someone takes on the strict purity rules of קודש for his חולין, that food can carry a שלישי. Eating it makes his body a שני, so he can pass impurity on to קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Third-degree impurity
Second-degree impurity
Ordinary, non-sacred food
Handled according to the purity standards of sacred food
His body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the food itself is קודש. It is ordinary חולין that someone chose to handle with the strict purity rules of קודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that taking on a higher purity standard can change how much impurity ordinary food is able to hold.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Asi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said that Rabbi Yannai said:
One who eats a third-degree item of non-sacred food
that were prepared with the purity of sacred food –
his body becomes second-degree for sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the purity level of תרומה to food handled with the stricter purity level of קודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of קודש makes the eater's body a שני for קודש.

steps.title: A teaching mentions only the purity of תרומה, implying not the purity of קודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a teaching that applies this rule only to חולין handled with the purity of תרומה. He reads that as excluding the purity of קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected to רבי אסי: 'A third-degree item makes one second-degree for sacred food, but not second-degree for תרומה, in the case of non-sacred food prepared with the purity of תרומה.' With the purity of תרומה, yes; with the purity of sacred food, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבי אסי. He quotes a teaching that speaks only about חולין handled with the purity of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted teaching says that eating such a שלישי makes a person a שני for קודש but not for תרומה. It only mentions חולין handled with the purity of תרומה. רבי זירא reads that as meaning the case of קודש purity is left out, which seems to clash with רבי ינאי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Yes
No

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection to Rabbi Asi:
A third-degree item makes one second-degree for sacred food,
but not second-degree for teruma,
in the case of non-sacred food prepared with the purity of teruma.
With the purity of teruma – yes,
phrases.notes: From here on, the גמרא is drawing a conclusion from the teaching's exact wording.

phrases.english: with the purity of sacred food – no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's ruling as reported by רבי אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that חולין handled with the purity of קודש can carry a שלישי that makes the eater a שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching mentions only the purity of תרומה. That suggests the rule does not hold for the purity of קודש.

steps.title: The teaching uses a 'no need to say' style
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers that the case of קודש purity is so obvious that the teaching did not need to mention it. It mentions the case of תרומה to teach that even this case works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the challenge. The teaching does not leave out קודש; that case is simply too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purity of קודש is stricter, so of course חולין handled that way can carry a שלישי. The teaching chose the less obvious case of תרומה purity to show that even there, the rule holds. So the inference from the teaching's wording falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (the obvious case goes without saying)
He is saying

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אסי, חולין handled with the purity of קודש can carry a שלישי, and eating it makes the body a שני for קודש. In his reading, the teaching that mentions תרומה only adds a less obvious case; it does not exclude קודש. Step 6 shows that not everyone reports רבי יוחנן this way.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a common pattern in the גמרא: a source that mentions only the less obvious case does not exclude the more obvious one.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style.
phrases.notes: He means it's obvious for קודש purity, which is stricter, so the teaching tells us that even תרומה purity works.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source with a 'לא מיבעיא' style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching's mention of תרומה purity excludes קודש purity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case of קודש purity is obvious; the teaching adds that even תרומה purity works, so רבי ינאי's ruling stands.

steps.title: A quote from רבי יהושע seems to limit the rule to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי: רבי יהושע himself said he was only talking about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהושע said, "I too only said this about תרומה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבי אסי's answer from Step 4. It brings a quote where רבי יהושע says his rule was only about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי said the case of קודש purity was too obvious to mention. But רבי יהושע's words "I only said it about תרומה" sound like he is limiting the rule to תרומה and leaving out קודש. That supports רבי זירא's reading from Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. This opens a challenge.
I too only said it about... This limits a statement.
He is saying.

phrases.english: But surely he says, "I too did not say it
phrases.notes: That's רבי יהושע, as רבה בר בר חנה reported him earlier in the name of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: except regarding תרומה" — that is what he says!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בִּתְרוּמָה״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אסי's answer in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's claim that the case of קודש purity was simply too obvious to mention.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע explicitly limits his statement to תרומה, which suggests the case of קודש purity is left out, not just left unsaid.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a dispute between אמוראים about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they disagree about the view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the two reports come from different אמוראים who explain רבי יוחנן differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה reported רבי יוחנן's version as limited to תרומה. רבי אסי understood רבי יוחנן's view to include קודש purity too. So the quote does not disprove רבי אסי. It is simply the other side of the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: They are אמוראים. This means there are two sages with two opinions, so one cannot disprove the other.
According to the view of. Here it describes what each one thinks a certain sage held.

phrases.english: They are אמוראים,
phrases.notes: He means רבה בר בר חנה and רבי אסי.

phrases.english: and they disagree about the view of רבי יוחנן.

steps.whatToRemember: Whether רבי יהושע's rule covers חולין handled with קודש purity depends on how you report רבי יוחנן. רבה בר בר חנה and רבי אסי disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between אמוראים: the challenging source reflects a different report of the same teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's words, as reported, disprove רבי אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those words reflect רבה בר בר חנה's report. רבי אסי holds a different understanding of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: עולא: Eating a שלישי disqualifies a person from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that someone who eats a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה may no longer eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Someone who eats a שלישי of חולין that were handled with the purity of תרומה becomes disqualified from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. עולא gives a ruling about a person who eats third-level impure food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שלישי does not ruin תרומה through touching. But עולא says that eating such food, when it was חולין kept at the purity of תרומה, makes the person's own body unfit to eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Third level of impurity.
The purity standard of תרומה. Here it means חולין that were handled as carefully as תרומה.
His body becomes disqualified.

phrases.english: עולא said:
One who eats a שלישי of חולין
that were prepared with the purity of תרומה —
his body is disqualified from eating תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement on the same topic of eating impure food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה disqualifies the eater from eating תרומה.

steps.title: Why did עולא need to say this? The משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עולא adds, since a משנה already implies that the eater becomes a שלישי for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: A שלישי makes the eater a שני for קודש but not a שני for תרומה, in the case of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה. He is not a שני, but he is a שלישי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's statement as unnecessary. It quotes a משנה that seems to say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the eater is not a שני for תרומה. The גמרא reads this precisely: not a שני, but still a שלישי. A שלישי disqualifies a person from תרומה, so עולא's rule seems to be already there.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? This asks why a statement is needed.
Second level of impurity.
Sacred food from the קרבנות. It needs the highest level of purity.
But, by implication. It introduces a precise reading of the words.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: a שלישי makes him a שני for קודש,
but not a שני for תרומה,
in the case of חולין prepared with the purity of תרומה.
It is a שני that he does not become,
but a שלישי he does become.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's statement as already taught in a משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A precise reading of the משנה ("not a שני" means "but a שלישי") already gives עולא's rule.

steps.title: Without עולא, we might have read the משנה differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from the משנה alone we might think the eater gets no impurity at all for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that משנה, I would have said he is neither a שני nor a שלישי. It only said "not a שני for תרומה" because it had just said "a שני for קודש." So עולא teaches us that he is a שלישי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. It shows that the משנה's wording could be read in a way that does not teach his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "not a שני for תרומה" might just be a matching phrase, said only because the משנה had said "a שני for קודש." Read that way, they would not imply that he is a שלישי. עולא tells us clearly that he is a שלישי and cannot eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: If we only had that source.
I would have said. This is the mistaken first thought.
Since it said... This means a phrase was added only to match an earlier phrase.

phrases.english: If from that one, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שֵׁנִי הָוֵי וְלָא שְׁלִישִׁי הָוֵי,
phrases.english: he is neither a שני nor a שלישי,
and since it said "a שני for קודש" —
it also said "not a שני for תרומה,"
so he teaches us.

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's point: eating a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה really does make the person a שלישי for תרומה. The משנה's wording alone was not clear enough to prove this.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's phrase "not a שני for תרומה" does not by itself prove he is a שלישי. It may just be a matching phrase. That is exactly why עולא was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Without עולא, the משנה would have been misread. Its wording could be a matching phrase rather than a precise limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the משנה alone: the eater is neither a שני nor a שלישי for תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא teaches that the eater is a שלישי and is disqualified from eating תרומה.

steps.title: The stew with תרומה spices challenges עולא
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a משנה that allows a שלישי of חולין to be eaten in a stew mixed with תרומה. If eating the שלישי disqualifies the eater from תרומה, this permission makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected to עולא from a משנה: first-degree חולין is impure and makes impure. Second-degree חולין disqualifies but does not make impure. Third-degree חולין may be eaten in a stew mixed with תרומה. Now, if you say that eating it disqualifies his body from eating תרומה, would we feed him something that disqualifies his own body?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא brings a משנה that seems to clash with עולא's ruling from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a כהן eat a שלישי of חולין in a stew that also contains תרומה. According to עולא, eating that שלישי would make the כהן unfit to eat תרומה. Then he would be eating the תרומה in that same stew while disqualified, so the משנה should never have allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: First-degree impurity: food that touched a primary source of impurity
Second-degree impurity
Disqualifies, but does not make the next item able to pass on impurity
A stew mixed with תרומה, such as תרומה spices
Ordinary, non-sacred food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts. The first part, from רִאשׁוֹן to נְזִיד הַדֶּמַע, is the quoted משנה. The part from וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ on is רב המנונא's own question built on that משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection to Ulla:
The first-degree impure food among non-sacred food
is impure and makes other things impure,
phrases.notes: In this משנה, 'makes impure' means it makes תרומה impure enough that the תרומה can disqualify other תרומה.

phrases.english: and the second-degree disqualifies but does not make impure,
and the third-degree may be eaten in a stew mixed with תרומה.
And if you say his body becomes disqualified
from eating תרומה,
would we feed him something
that disqualifies his own body?
phrases.notes: He means the תרומה in that same stew: once he eats the שלישי, he couldn't eat that תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Steps 8 and 9 clarified what עולא adds, a new challenge now attacks his ruling directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that someone who eats a שלישי of חולין handled with the purity of תרומה may no longer eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows a שלישי to be eaten together with תרומה in one stew. If eating the שלישי disqualified the eater, the משנה would be feeding him תרומה while he is unfit to eat it.

steps.title: עולא sets the stew case aside
steps.stepSummary: עולא starts his answer by telling רב המנונא to leave the stew case aside. This hints that the stew is a special case that does not disprove his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Leave aside the stew mixed with תרומה,
steps.whatsHappening: עולא begins his answer. He is setting up an explanation of why the stew case is different, and that explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not take back his ruling. He says the stew is not a fair test of it, because something about that case makes it an exception. The reason itself comes in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside, meaning 'that case is different, do not compare it'

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside the stew mixed with תרומה,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא responds to רב המנונא's challenge from the stew.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the stew is treated as an exception that cannot refute the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה about the stew seemed to show that eating a שלישי does not disqualify the eater from תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stew is a special case, so עולא's general ruling still stands. The reason is explained in the continuation.
